# Counters

Every counter Cavalry has, from `counters.toml`, the single source ([ADR 0012](../decisions/0012-lay-out-the-counters-file.md)). The driver publishes each one in the [counters file](counters-file.md). A static counter is allocated when the file is created, in the record whose index is its id, and its label is its name. An instance counter is allocated per key when its instance is created, and its label is the name, a space, and the key's text as the doc column defines it. A client counter is allocated per key when a client adds it with `add counter`, with the key and the label the client gives; the client alone writes its value, and the driver frees it when the client removes it, closes or is timed out ([ADR 0062](../decisions/0062-add-a-clients-counter-with-aerons-counter-commands.md)). A `counter` never decreases while allocated; a `gauge` moves both ways. This page is generated by `scripts/gen-counters.py`: edit `counters.toml`, never this page, and `just lint-counters` fails when the two differ.

| Id | Name | Kind | Scope | What a change means | What to do |

A leader told this member that its log, below a position this member knows to be committed, is not the leader's: one of the two holds a log that is not this cluster's, a log directory copied from another cluster or restored from an older copy. | 135 | `cluster.log_replications` | counter | client | Times one cluster member replicated, or served, a span of the log below the leader's term base log position, a term the member missed: on a follower, a catch-up position it sent from follower log replication; on the leader, a replay of its own recordings that it started for such a member, once for each replay where the span lies in several recordings (spec/cluster.md, follower log replication, Messages outside an election, and Counters; ADR 0085, ADR 0086); key: member id (i32), little-endian; label text: the member id in decimal. | A member that was down or cut off while the cluster elected a leader replicates the terms it missed from the new leader's recordings. This rises by one on the member for each term it asks for, and by one on the leader for each replay it starts, which is one for each recording the term lies in. It is how such a member returns, and nothing to act on. If it rises on a leader again and again for one member while that member's cluster.append_position does not move, the member cannot receive the replay: check that its catchup endpoint in the members string is the one its host listens on and that the leader's host can reach it. |
| 136 | `cluster.log_replications_unavailable` | counter | client | Times one cluster member failed its election in follower log replication because its append position stayed below its stop position without moving for the leader heartbeat timeout: the leader's recordings do not hold the span, purged by retention, a replay stopped for a fault, or the replay never reached the member's catchup endpoint. Counted in cluster.elections_failed too (spec/cluster.md, follower log replication, and Counters; ADR 0086); key: member id (i32), little-endian; label text: the member id in decimal. | This member asked its leader for a term it missed and nothing more arrived for 10 s. Check, on the leader's host, that its recordings still hold the log from this member's cluster.append_position: where a retention purged it, this member cannot rejoin from the log at all, and this version has no snapshot to bring it back with, so the leader's log must be kept until every member has it. Check that this member's catchup endpoint in the members string is the same on both hosts and that the leader's host can reach it: a leader replays to the endpoint its own members string names. If cluster.log_replications rises on the leader for this member each time, the replays start and do not arrive. |
| 137 | `cluster.catchups` | counter | client | Times one cluster member began, or served, a catch-up within the leader's term: on a follower, a catch-up position it sent from follower catch-up init; on the leader, a replay of its live recording that it started for such a member, which follows the recording until the leader stops it (spec/cluster.md, follower catch-up init, Messages outside an election, and Counters; ADR 0087, ADR 0088); key: member id (i32), little-endian; label text: the member id in decimal. | A member that joined its leader's term behind the leader's log catches up from the leader's live recording, and this rises on both by one. It is how such a member returns, and nothing to act on. If it rises on a leader again and again for one member while that member's cluster.append_position does not reach the leader's, the member cannot keep up with the replay or cannot receive it: check that its catchup endpoint in the members string is the one its host listens on, and compare its cluster.append_position with the leader's over a few seconds. |

## State machines

Every state machine on the data plane registers its states and transitions in `counters.toml` too, and `just lint-counters` fails a transition that names no counter, a counter that is not of kind `counter` in the table above, a counter whose constant no code in the enum's crate names, or an enum whose variants are not the machine's states (CLAUDE.md, invariant 4). The enum that holds the states carries the comment `// state machine: <name>` on the line before its definition. The check fails closed: every enum under `crates/*/src` whose name is or ends in `State`, `Status` or `Phase` carries that comment, or `// not a state machine: <why>` with the reason no transition of it needs a counter, and `just lint-counters` names the file and line of one that has neither. Each machine is listed here with the counter every transition adds one to.

### `counters_record`

States: `unused`, `allocated`, `reclaimed`.

| From | To | Counter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unused` | `allocated` | `counters.allocations` |
| `reclaimed` | `allocated` | `counters.allocations` |
| `allocated` | `reclaimed` | `counters.freed` |
